rules.statement: The metastability model is a simulation-only SystemVerilog model, not bound by the RTL rules, and must never be used for synthesis.
The RTL contains no elaboration check for parameter values; behavior with an illegal parameter value is undefined.
Defaults are 2 synchronizer stages, depth 8, data width 32; depth is a power of 2 with no upper limit, data width minimum 1 with no upper limit.
o_rd_data must always show the word at the current read pointer (show-ahead read), including while empty; there is no o_rd_valid.
o_full_thr must be 1 when occupancy >= i_full_thr; all i_full_thr values are accepted with no legal-range restriction.
o_empty_thr must be 1 when occupancy <= i_empty_thr; all i_empty_thr values are accepted with no legal-range restriction.
The threshold inputs i_full_thr and i_empty_thr are static, written once before use.

rules.condition: after a rejected write or read request
rules.statement: o_overflow and o_underflow must be registered 1-cycle pulses appearing in the cycle after the rejected request.
An underflow read must not change the read pointer, and o_rd_data keeps showing the word at the read pointer.
The write and read domain resets (asynchronous assert, active low) need not be asserted at the same time, and clock frequencies and ratio are unrestricted.
Each synchronizer bit has its own reset value (vector).
The model randomizes each bit's latency independently as S-1, S or S+1 cycles after the first capturing edge; a new input change during the delay replaces the pending change and restarts the delay.
The metastability model is controlled by plusargs for seed and enable.
The SRAM wrapper and model implement a generic one-write-port, one-read-port foundry-style interface.
The FIFO array is a separate module modelled as a one-write, one-read SRAM, and the top instantiates the write module, read module and array module.
The full, empty and threshold flags must be combinational from the synchronized pointers.

Timing exceptions: set_max_delay 0.9 x write clock period for the write pointer, 0.9 x read clock period for the read pointer, 1 x read clock period for the data path; static thresholds use a false path; no set_min_delay.

The macro VLSIT_SYNTHESIS selects branches only in m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync: with the macro is the synthesizable model, without is the simulation model; simulation defines it for the synthesizable branch, synthesis and analysis flows define it.
Storage read is synchronous: the read module drives the next read pointer address, storage is read every read-clock cycle, o_rd_data is the storage output, with no memory read enable.
The software reset input i_rst_n_sw is active-low level (0 = reset requested), idle value 1, synchronous to i_clk_wr and sampled at the clock, not an asynchronous reset.
i_rst_n_sw may be low for one write-clock cycle or any longer time; the FSM latches the request and waits in HOLD while it is low.
o_sw_rst_busy must be driven directly by a flip-flop with no combinational logic on the output path.

rules.condition: while the write side is blocked by software reset
rules.statement: o_full must be 1 while the write side is blocked by the software reset and return to normal full logic at write release.

rules.condition: write or read blocked by software reset
rules.statement: A write or read blocked by the software reset must not raise an o_overflow or o_underflow pulse.
While blocked, o_full_thr and o_empty_thr must take the values of an empty FIFO.
The write block is combinational (zero latency) from i_rst_n_sw and the FSM state, adding a combinational path to write accept and memory write enable.

rules.condition: hardware reset and software reset conflict
rules.statement: Hardware resets have priority over the software reset; a hardware reset of one domain only during the sequence is not repaired.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while write FSM is in REL
rules.statement: Writes stay blocked and a new sequence starts when the FSM is back in RUN.
The request and acknowledge crossings use set_max_delay of 0.9 x the source clock period.
A side is released only when the synchronized pointer of the other side is 0.
The software reset must not clear the storage; only pointers and flags are reset.
Both clocks run during the whole software reset; there is no timeout.
PARA_AFIFO_CELL_TYPE selects the cell: 0 bypass, 1 two D-FF cells, 2 one 2-FF cell, 3 one 3-FF cell, 4 one 4-FF cell; above 4 gives the 4-FF cell; default 2.
Option 0 (bypass) is not legal for the pointer crossings.

The metastability model lives only in the simulation branch of m_vlsit_afifo_cell_sync; m_vlsit_afifo_sync only instantiates one cell wrapper per bit, and other modules only instantiate m_vlsit_afifo_sync.
Instance names of cells and macros follow u_dont_touch_.
Example cell models are synthesizable RTL, one module per file in 000_Common/rtl_cells, with pins CK, RN or SN, D, Q, exempt from the naming rule; the SRAM model stays simulation-only per DEC-040.
VLSIT_CELL_SRAM_1W1R is synthesizable RTL with parameters ADDR_W and DATA_W, bit write mask BWEB, read register QR, no reset; a same-edge read of a written address returns the old word.
Library wrappers, cells and macro models are written in common_rtl/000_Common (rtl_lib and rtl_cells), each folder with its own filelist.f.
RTL module port lists are aligned in four columns and declared in functional groups with a comment per group, clock and reset first.
Cell and macro models are named VLSIT_CELL_*, and the header states that the model is synthesizable RTL and a real design uses the synthesis-library cell.
